body:
Hello cooperative members,

Here is the release note for the changes now available across the Alderbridge Learning Cooperative course catalogue and enrollment workspace. These updates were shaped by reports from learners, instructors, and enrollment coordinators during the winter term. They are in place for all active courses; no action is needed to keep existing enrollments.

COURSE CATALOGUE

• Course pages now show the next available section beside the course title, including its start date, meeting pattern, delivery format, and remaining-seat status. When a course has several sections, learners can compare them without returning to the search results. A section marked “Waitlist” remains visible, but its status is no longer mistaken for an open seat.

• Catalogue filters now stay in place when a learner opens a course and returns to the results. Filters include subject area, level, language of instruction, and online or in-person format. The results count updates when a filter changes, and a clear-filters control removes the whole set at once. Search still includes course descriptions and instructor-provided keywords.

• Course pages now distinguish required materials from suggested preparation. Instructors can also add a short note explaining whether a listed item is supplied by the cooperative. Existing material lists have been retained, though a few older entries may display under “Suggested preparation” until their course team reviews them.

ENROLLMENT AND ROSTERS

• The enrollment form now saves progress between steps. Learners can review contact details, section selection, and any course-specific questions on one confirmation screen before submitting. A saved form is kept for 14 days on the same account; it is not a completed enrollment, and seats are not held while a form is saved.

• If a selected section fills before submission, the form now explains what changed and offers the waitlist option where one is available. It will not silently switch a learner to a different time or section. Duplicate submissions for the same learner and section are also blocked with a link to the existing enrollment record.

• Coordinators can now export a roster with separate columns for enrollment status, waitlist position, accommodation request status, and last-updated date. The export omits private notes and answers to course questions by default. Those details remain available only in the learner’s record to staff with the appropriate permission.

• Instructors can mark attendance from the roster on a phone or tablet, and the roster keeps the selected class date while moving between learners. Attendance changes are recorded with the editor and timestamp. This does not change enrollment status or automatically notify a learner.

ACCESSIBILITY AND ACCOUNT DETAILS

• Keyboard focus is now more visible in the catalogue, enrollment steps, and roster tools. Form errors are announced next to the field that needs attention, and the enrollment confirmation includes a concise status summary for screen readers.

• Learners can update their preferred name independently of the name used for receipts and official enrollment records. Coordinators will see both labels where needed; instructors see the preferred name on their class roster. Changing a preferred name does not alter past records.

A few details worth noting: the new remaining-seat indicator refreshes when a course page is loaded, rather than continuously. A section can therefore fill between viewing the page and submitting a form; the updated check at submission will show the current status. Roster exports use the time zone configured for the cooperative, while the account activity record stores timestamps in a consistent system format.

We have also corrected a handful of smaller issues: course dates no longer shift by a day for some learners outside the cooperative’s time zone; long course titles wrap in the mobile catalogue; and the enrollment receipt now names the selected section rather than only the course. Existing receipts and saved rosters have not been rewritten.

If something looks wrong in a particular course or enrollment, reply with the course title and section code, but please do not include sensitive learner details in email. The support team can follow up through the cooperative’s usual account channel.

Regards,
Mara Venn
Product coordinator
Alderbridge Learning Cooperative
https://help.alderbridge.example.org/releases

--
Small display note: one older mail client may show “&” in a course title where the title contains an ampersand. The catalogue itself displays the title correctly.

Hello everyone,

We shipped a set of changes to the Fieldnote workspace this morning. These are all available now; there’s nothing to enable, and existing project links and exports are unchanged.

**A clearer handoff between intake and review**

Intake records now have a distinct “Ready for review” state. Moving a record into that state preserves the original submission date and records who made the handoff, so coordinators can see both the age of a request and when it was actually ready for a researcher. The review queue can also be filtered by study and assigned reviewer. We added a small warning when a record is moved while required consent details are still missing; the warning explains what’s incomplete rather than blocking the handoff.

**Batch updates for participant logistics**

Coordinators can now select several participants and update their contact status or visit window in one operation. The confirmation screen lists the records that will change before anything is saved. If a selected record has been edited by someone else since the list was opened, it’s left untouched and called out in the results, rather than overwriting the newer edit. The activity history records each successful change separately, including the person who made it.

**A more useful export preview**

The export preview now shows the fields and filters that will be included in a CSV before you download it. Hidden internal notes stay excluded by default, and the preview calls that out explicitly. Date values follow the format selected in workspace settings, while blank optional fields remain blank instead of being filled with a placeholder. This should make it easier to spot a mistaken filter before a file leaves the workspace.

**Notes that keep their context**

A note can now be attached to a specific visit as well as to a participant. Visit-linked notes appear in the visit timeline and in the participant’s overall history, with a label showing where they were entered. Existing notes haven’t been changed. We’ve also added a compact indicator when a note was edited after it was first saved; the full edit history remains available to workspace administrators.

**Small fixes and tidy-ups**

- The queue no longer jumps back to the first page after an assignment is changed.
- Search now matches hyphenated study codes whether or not the hyphen is included.
- The consent summary uses the current protocol title rather than a title copied when the record was created.
- Screen readers now announce when a filter has been applied or cleared.
- Downloaded filenames include the study code when one is set, which helps when several exports land in the same folder.

We’ve kept the changes deliberately narrow. In particular, participant permissions and retention settings have not changed, and no new fields are required for existing studies. If a result looks unexpected, reply with the study code and a short description of what you were doing; please leave participant names and contact details out of email.

Thanks,
Mara
Research Operations
Lattice Grove Studio

body:
Hi everyone,

We shipped a set of changes to the Fieldnote workspace this morning. They’re focused on the everyday handoffs between study setup, fieldwork, and the people who keep an eye on the records. Nothing to configure before using them; the updated controls are available in your workspace now.

**Study intake can now be reviewed in one pass**

The intake queue has a new review view that brings the request, its attached materials, and the assigned study lead together on one screen. Reviewers can leave a note on an individual answer, mark a section as needing clarification, or return the whole request with a short explanation. The requester sees the notes beside the relevant fields rather than in a separate email thread.

We also added a small but useful safeguard: changing the study lead no longer clears the intake review status. The previous lead’s comments remain in the activity history, so the new owner can pick up without asking someone to forward context.

**Fieldwork status is easier to scan**

The study list now shows the latest fieldwork update and when it was recorded. You can filter by studies with no update in the past seven days, or by a specific collection phase. The date shown is the date of the update itself, not the date someone opened the study, which should make routine check-ins a little less ambiguous.

For teams that use participant groups, the group name is now included in the export summary. This applies to both CSV downloads and the printable study snapshot. Existing column selections are retained when you download again.

**A clearer trail for record changes**

The activity panel now distinguishes edits to a record from edits to its status. It shows who made the change, the time, and the fields affected. When a value is replaced, the earlier value is available in the history for workspace members who have access to that study. We’ve also corrected the display for changes made shortly before midnight: the activity time now follows the workspace time zone consistently.

**A couple of smaller fixes**

- Long study names no longer push the owner and phase out of alignment in the list.
- Uploading a second attachment with the same filename produces a clear prompt instead of silently replacing the first file.
- The reminder setting now stays off when a study is copied from a template where reminders were disabled.

A note on the intake review change: requests already in progress keep their current status. You can open one and use the new review view without restarting it. The fieldwork filters may take a moment to appear for workspaces with a large number of archived studies; the list itself remains available while they load.

Thanks to the teams who sent us examples of the handoff gaps and export inconsistencies. Those reports helped us make these changes specific to the work, rather than adding another layer of process.

Mara
Research Operations
North Quay Research Studio
mara@northquay.example.org

Meridian Vale Housing Services
Service update bulletin · 18 September 2025
Release reference: MVH-OPS-25.09.3
Applies to: Tenant Portal, account services and regional operations teams

Dear residents and account contacts,

The following changes were released to the Meridian Vale Housing Services portal on 16 September. They are available to accounts in all service districts unless an item below notes otherwise. No action is required for most changes. Existing case numbers, submitted documents and scheduled appointments remain unchanged.

TENANT PORTAL

1. Clearer repair appointment updates
Repair requests now show the most recent appointment status and the date it was updated. When a visit is moved, the request history displays both the previous window and the replacement window. This makes it easier to distinguish a confirmed appointment from a requested change. The update applies to requests opened on or after 3 June 2024; older requests retain their existing history view. Confirmation notices continue to be sent by email where an address is on file.

2. Document receipt confirmation
After a resident uploads a file to an open case, the case page now displays the file name, upload time and a receipt status. A status of “Received” confirms that the file reached the case record; it does not indicate that the document has been reviewed or accepted. If an upload is interrupted, the page will show that the receipt is incomplete and provide a link to try again. Accepted file types and the existing 20 MB per-file limit have not changed.

3. Household contact details
The account details page now separates the primary contact number from an optional alternate number. Residents can update either field without replacing the other. Changes are recorded in the account activity history with the date submitted. For a joint account, a change to the primary contact number is visible to all authorized account holders. This does not change emergency contact information held separately by a housing team.

ACCOUNT SERVICES

4. Payment allocation history
The payment history now includes a “How this was applied” detail for transactions posted from 1 August 2025 onward. Where a payment covers more than one charge, the detail lists the allocation date and the affected account entries. Pending card payments are still shown separately and may not appear in the allocation history until settlement. The displayed amount and posting date continue to follow the account ledger; this release does not alter balances or payment arrangements.

5. Statements available in accessible formats
Monthly account statements can now be opened as tagged PDF files, with headings and table labels recognized by common screen readers. The standard PDF remains available from the same statement row. Previously issued statements have not been regenerated. Residents who need a statement in another format can contact the account team and quote the statement month and account reference; please do not include full payment card details in a message.

6. Case reference in correspondence
Automated account-service emails now include the case reference in the subject line when a message relates to an existing enquiry. Replies to those notices will continue to attach to the case when sent from the email address registered on the account. If the registered address has changed, use the portal to update it or contact the service desk so staff can verify the account before changing correspondence details.

STAFF AND REGIONAL OPERATIONS

7. District hand-off notes
Housing officers can now add a concise hand-off note when transferring an open case between district queues. The note is recorded with the transfer date and staff reference, and is visible to authorized staff working on that case. Tenant-facing case pages do not display internal hand-off notes. Existing privacy and access rules continue to apply; information not needed to resolve a case should not be entered in the note.

8. Duplicate enquiry review
The operations queue now flags possible duplicate enquiries when the account reference and case category match an item received within the previous 14 days. The flag is a review aid only: it does not merge cases or prevent staff from opening a new record. Staff must confirm that the enquiries concern the same issue before linking them. Residents may therefore still receive separate case references for separate repair or account matters.

KNOWN LIMITATION

Some older Android devices may return to the account overview after a resident downloads a statement. The statement file is still saved to the device when the download completes. If the page returns before completion, open the statement again using a stable connection. The portal team is reviewing this behavior; no account information or statement content is affected.

SERVICE STATUS AND SUPPORT

Portal services remained available during deployment. A short delay in payment-history updates was observed between 06:40 and 07:05 on 16 September; entries received during that period were subsequently processed. If a recent transaction is still missing, allow up to two working days for posting before contacting the account team.

Residents can review current cases and account information at https://portal.meridianvale.example.org/account. For a repair or housing enquiry, use https://portal.meridianvale.example.org/cases. The service-status page is https://status.meridianvale.example.org. Please access these addresses directly rather than sending passwords or verification codes by email.

If you contact us about an item in this bulletin, include the release reference MVH-OPS-25.09.3 and the relevant case or account reference. Do not send identity documents unless a housing officer has requested them through an approved channel.

This notice describes portal and service-process changes only. Your tenancy terms, rent charges, eligibility decisions and existing service appointments are not changed by this release.

Regards,

Leena Voss
Service Operations Manager
Meridian Vale Housing Services
serviceupdates@meridianvale.example.org
https://www.meridianvale.example.org

Meridian Vale Housing Services · Regional Service Bulletin
Please retain this notice for reference. This mailbox is monitored for delivery issues; case-specific requests should be submitted through the portal.

NORTHBANK REGIONAL HOUSING SERVICE
Service update | 18 June 2025
Release bulletin: tenant and account operations
Reference: NRHS-RB-25-06

Dear tenant,

The following changes are now available in the Northbank Regional Housing Service account. They apply to active residential tenancies managed by Northbank and do not change rent amounts, payment dates, tenancy terms or existing service arrangements. The dates below indicate when each change was made available.

1. Payment history now includes reference details
Released 3 June 2025 | Account service 4.18.2

The Payments page now displays the receipt date, amount, payment method and the reference assigned to each recorded transaction. Where a payment is still being matched to an account, its status is shown as “Processing” rather than appearing as a completed receipt. Once matched, the receipt is added to the same history without requiring a separate request.

This display covers payments recorded from 1 January 2024 onward. Older transactions remain available through the existing statement request process. A scheduled payment may take up to two working days to appear, depending on the payment provider and bank processing times.

2. Household contact details can be reviewed separately
Released 6 June 2025 | Account service 4.18.4

The Contact details section now distinguishes the primary correspondence address from the address of the rented home. Tenants can review the correspondence address and telephone number held for their account. Changes submitted by one named account holder are marked as pending until the service team has completed its standard verification.

The rented-home address is read-only. To report an error in that address, use the Repairs and tenancy enquiries form so the request can be checked against the tenancy record. Updating contact details does not amend the names of tenants on a tenancy agreement.

3. Repair request status has additional milestones
Released 11 June 2025 | Repairs service 2.7.0

Repair requests now show separate milestones for “Received,” “Assigned,” “Appointment proposed” and “Work recorded.” Previously submitted requests retain their existing reference numbers; their current status is displayed using the updated milestones where applicable. The status describes the latest recorded action and is not a confirmation that a contractor has attended unless the page explicitly says “Work recorded.”

Appointment proposals continue to be sent through the contact method selected for the request. Tenants who cannot attend a proposed appointment should reply using the instructions in that message. Emergency reporting arrangements are unchanged; the account status page is not monitored as an emergency reporting channel.

4. Monthly account statements are easier to download
Released 16 June 2025 | Documents service 1.12.1

Statements are now listed by statement month and document date, with a separate download control for each available PDF. The page also identifies a statement that has been regenerated following a correction. A regenerated file replaces the earlier version for that period; the document date indicates when the current file was issued.

Statements are provided for account information and do not replace formal notices served under a tenancy agreement. If a document appears to relate to a different household, do not forward it. Contact the service team using the details below and include the document reference, but not bank card details or account passwords.

Account links
Sign in: https://accounts.northbank.example.org/sign-in
Payments and statements: https://accounts.northbank.example.org/account/documents
Repairs and tenancy enquiries: https://accounts.northbank.example.org/help/requests
Service status: https://status.northbank.example.org

These pages may require sign-in. For your security, Northbank staff will not ask you to send your password by email. If you use a shared device, sign out when you have finished and close the browser window.

Questions about an account record may be sent to accountdesk@northbank.example.org or raised by telephone at 01632 960 418, Monday to Friday, 09:00–17:00. Please quote reference NRHS-RB-25-06 if you contact us about this bulletin. Do not include sensitive personal information unless it is necessary to identify the record concerned.

Regards,

Mara Ellison
Service Operations Manager
Northbank Regional Housing Service
https://www.northbank.example.org
